example: A definition named `glossary.first_parent_history` declares the phrase "first-parent history". A term reference to that name renders the phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to the declaration, without displaying the identifier or a badge. {cite}`requirements.definitions.references`
rationale: Two tests in `tests/definitions.rs` carry `{test}` references to the example. - **`a_term_reference_renders_only_its_phrase_as_a_plain_link`** (lines 328–358) reproduces the example's scenario exactly. - Setup: it declares the definition `glossary.first_parent_history` with the phrase "first-parent history". A second chapter contains a `{term}` reference to that name. - Assertion on the guide chapter: it asserts the whole rendered guide chapter equals `Follow the first-parent history.` - That output is an ordinary hyperlink with no class, badge image or other markup. - The phrase is the only link text, and the identifier is not displayed. - The link points at the anchored declaration. - Assertion on the glossary chapter: it asserts the anchor `id="habeas-definition-glossary.first_parent_history"` exists there. - **`phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved`** (lines 291–326) adds related coverage. - It asserts that no `shields.io` badge appears. - It asserts that exactly one link is produced, with a relative `../glossary.html#...` href. Escaped references and references inside code examples stay literal, which is why only one link appears. - It asserts that the phrase is escaped for rendering (`*alpha* & <beta>`). - It asserts that the `:phrase:` field does not leak into the declaration. Together, the setup and assertions cover the example's scenario and expected outcome.

text: A definition named `glossary.first_parent_history` declares the phrase "first-parent history". A term reference to that name renders the phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to the declaration, without displaying the identifier or a badge. {cite}`requirements.definitions.references`

The `{term}` role followed by a backtick-delimited full definition name MUST reference a named definition. In rendered Markdown, the reference MUST display the definition's phrase as an ordinary hyperlink to its anchored declaration, without a badge. The phrase MUST be escaped appropriately for rendering.

Missing targets and targets of another kind MUST be reported. Escaped references and references in Markdown code examples MUST remain literal. A term reference MUST NOT satisfy a requirement citation or a Rust function's requirement-coverage obligation.
